occursIn.locator: Lemma I.4.21 (f' ~ r^{-1}(af+h) with h non-negligible).
occursIn.note: Same hypotheses (a>0; h positive, measurable, regularly varying of index b>0; f differentiable with f'(r) ~ (af(r)+h(r))/r; b>a) and both conclusions (f ~ h/(b-a); f eventually positive and regularly varying of index b on a half-line). Domain (0,infinity) for h as in the source; the same domain for f, which the source leaves implicit.

proofUses.reason: A regularly varying integrating factor and a positive forcing-index gap identify signed asymptotics without differentiating the normalization.
The proof transforms the equation to a linear one for w=u^{-gamma} and solves it with an integrating factor; it invokes no other wiki assertion.
The proof inverts the scale s(r) and substitutes F(t)^alpha into the cutoff-to-full transfer theorem (9PSJ) with its coefficient c_*.
The proof integrates the transformed linear equation w'=a gamma C directly; it invokes no other wiki assertion.
The proof solves the explicit linear equation w'-w/t=a gamma C in closed form; it invokes no other wiki assertion.

The asymptotic relation becomes the exact equation rf'=(1-theta)(af+h) with theta->0; after local boundedness of h (uniform convergence theorem) and local absolute continuity of f, the signed linear theorem 2KB9 with A=1 gives f/h->1/(b-a), and regular variation of f follows from that of h (3491).
